subject: Need advice on adjusting hyperparameters for mixed effects model

messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Need advice on adjusting hyperparameters for mixed effects model
parts:
Hello,

I'm attempting to replicate the structure of a Stan model in INLA (Really looking forward to INLA's speed!)

This is a mixed effects model on score for individuals, each with repeated measures.  There are a few fixed and random effects.  I attempted fitting with all the priors left to default, but after 10 hours of running, and multiple warnings about Hessian problems, killed the process.  We have strong domain knowledge on this study, so it would make sense to manually tune some of the hyper-parameters/priors to help INLA. (i.e. the intercept should be around 11, and the random_effects should each be small, with mean 0 and maybe sd around 1)

While this is easy in Stan, I can't figure out how to do the same thing with INLA.

Here is the basic model.  Can anybody offer some guidance on how to adjust the hyper-parameters/priors for the random (group) effects?

subject_id2 <- subject_id
model_test <- inla(score ~ 1  + factor_1 + factor_2 + I(factor_2^2)
                        + f(rand_effect_1, model="iid")
                        + f(rand_effect_2, model="iid")
                        + f(subject_id, model="iid") + f(test_seq, replicate=subject_id2, model="ar1")
                       , data=df, family="gamma", control.compute=list(config = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

# Note:  test_seq is in integer that increments for each subject when they take the test.  Can think of it as a measure of each subject's experience

I'm also not 100% sure the last line is correct.  My intent is to have a slope per-subject, and then an autoregressive term for each subject that is AR1 (Their score/ability evolves over time.)

Does this model look correct for the subject intercept and AR term?
How/where can I adjust the hyper-parameters / priors for the 4 random effects (rand_effect_1, rand_effect_2, subject_id, test_seq)

Thank You!

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Need advice on adjusting hyperparameters for mixed effects model
parts:
A few tricks you can try:

## Priors
If you don't know what priors to use, use the pc priors, e.g.
hyper1 = list(theta = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(1,0.01)))
formula1 = y ~ f(plate, model="iid", hyper=hyper1)
(see https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic106.html)

And similarly for the ar1 process (https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic117.html).

## Factors
I suggest coding all of the factors manually as 0-1 covariates (one for each factor level). Whether you remove the intercept or not depends on how you code the factors. The easiest way to be absolutely sure you know what is going on with factors is to do the manual work.

## Fixed effects
You can use control.fixed to set the priors for these.

## Logfile
Please attache the output of the verbose=T, or the fit$logfile in future emails.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: Need advice on adjusting hyperparameters for mixed effects model
parts:
Another trick related to computing time during model development:

When developing the model and troubleshooting you can try -  
control.inla=list(int.strategy="eb") to get empirical Bayes results much faster.

When you get the model more or less the way you want it, you can switch to -
control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="auto") for a good balance between rigor and speed.

messages.subject: Re: Need advice on adjusting hyperparameters for mixed effects model
parts:
Here is some R code for messing with priors in a simple hierarchical regression model.

# some code for messing around with priors for simple hierarchical
# regression model. read "Spatial and Spatio-temporal Bayesian Models
# with R-INLA" for more info.

# set up
library(INLA)
library(inlabru)
library(brinla)
set.seed(123)

# start making data
m <- 1000 # sample size
set.seed(123)
x <- runif(m, 10, 50) # independent var
grp <- sample(seq(1, 10), size=m, replace=T) # groups

# simulate random intercept
tau.grp <- 0.01 # set precision
(sigma.grp <- sqrt(1/tau.grp)) # as standard deviation
set.seed(4455)
v <- rnorm(length(unique(grp)), 0, sqrt(1/tau.grp)) # random intercept
vj <- v[grp] # assign effect to individuals

# simulate y
tau.meas <- 0.04 # measurement error
(sigma.meas <- sqrt(1/tau.meas))
b0 <- 5 # intercept
beta1 <- 1.5 # slope
set.seed(334455)
y <- rnorm(m, b0 + vj + beta1*x, 1/sqrt(tau.meas)) # make response
dat1 <- data.frame(x, y, grp)

# plot it
ggplot(data=dat1, aes(x, y, col=factor(grp))) + geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm")

# define and run model with default priors, where prior for global intercept
# is norm(0, 0), global x effect is norm(0, 0.0001), and tau.grp is
# loggamma(1, 0.00005), I think.
form1 <- y ~ 1 + x + f(grp, model="iid")
out1 <- inla(form1, family="gaussian", data=dat1,
             control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", # balance speed, precision
                               int.strategy="auto"),
             control.compute=list(config=T), # for posterior sampling
             num.threads=3, # control number threads
             verbose=T)
summary(out1); plot(out1)
bri.hyperpar.summary(out1)

# define and run model with specified priors, where prior for global intercept
# is norm(0, 0.01), global x effect is norm(0, 0.01), and tau.grp is pc.prior
# with U=30 and alpha=0.01 (see https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.4630, page 14)
hyper2 = list(theta = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(30, 0.01)))
form2 <- y ~ 1 + x + f(grp, model="iid", hyper=hyper2)
out2 <- inla(form2 , family="gaussian", data=dat1,
             control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=0, # intercept
                                prec.intercept=0.01,
                                mean=0, # other global effects
                                prec=0.01),
             control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive",
                               int.strategy="auto"),
             control.compute=list(config=T),
             num.threads=3,
             verbose=T)
summary(out2); plot(out2)
bri.hyperpar.summary(out2)

# define and run model with specified priors, where prior for global intercept
# is norm(0, 0.01), global x effect is norm(0, 0.01), and tau.grp is
# loggamma(0.001, 0.001)
hyper3 <- list(theta=list(prior="loggamma", param=c(0.001, 0.001)))
form3 <- y ~ 1 + x + f(grp, model="iid", hyper=hyper3)
out3 <- inla(form3, family="gaussian", data=dat1,
             control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=0,
                                prec.intercept=0.01,
                                mean=0,
                                prec=0.01),
             control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive",
                               int.strategy="auto"),
             control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
             num.threads=3,
             verbose=T)
summary(out3)
bri.hyperpar.summary(out3)

# define and run model with specified priors, where prior for global intercept
# is norm(0, 0.01), global x effect is norm(0, 0.01), and tau.grp is
# a uniform-ish prior between 5 and 15
# simulate and specify tau.grp prior
a1 <- 5 # speculated lower bound for sigma.grp
b1 <- 15 # speculated upper bound for sigma.grp
sigma.grp <- runif(n=10000, min=a1, max=b1) # simulated standard deviation
tau.grp <- 1/(sigma.grp^2) # simulated precision
mean(tau.grp)
(a2 <- mean(tau.grp)^2 / var(tau.grp)) # transform parameters
(b2 <- a2 / mean(tau.grp)) # transform parameters
# define prior and formula
hyper4 <- list(theta=list(prec=list(prior="loggamma",
                                    param=c(a2, b2))))
form4 <- y ~ 1 + x + f(grp, model="iid", hyper=hyper4)
out4 <- inla(form4, family="gaussian", data=data.frame(x,y,grp),
             control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=0,
                                prec.intercept=0.01,
                                mean=0,
                                prec=0.01),
             control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive",
                               int.strategy="auto"),
             control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
             num.threads=3,
             verbose=T)
summary(out4); plot(out4)
bri.hyperpar.summary(out4)

# for more info
inla.list.models()
inla.list.models("prior")
inla.models()
inla.models()$latent$iid$hyper
inla.doc("pc.prec")
inla.set.control.fixed.default()

messages.subject: Re: Need advice on adjusting hyperparameters for mixed effects model
parts: One more thing. In the code above, you see how to modify the prior for all fixed effects at once. If you want to modify the prior for each fixed effect separately, note that in R-INLA:
y ~ 1 + x

describes the same model as

y ~ 1 + f(x, model="linear").

You can use the second syntax and add in any hyper argument you want. At least I think this is true, I haven't tested it.

On 14 Dec 2018, at 17:32, TDM <tme...@gmail.com> wrote:

One more thing. In the code above, you see how to modify the prior for all fixed effects at once. If you want to modify the prior for each fixed effect separately, note that in R-INLA:

y ~ 1 + x

describes the same model as

y ~ 1 + f(x, model="linear").

You can use the second syntax and add in any hyper argument you want. At least I think this is true, I haven't tested it.

Almost. You need

y ~ 1 + f(x, model=“linear”, prec.linear = somevalue)

The prior that needs specifying isn’t for a “hyperparameter” but rather
for the latent Gaussian variable itself, so “hyper” isn’t applicable.

Some more discussion of this can be found here:
https://github.com/fbachl/inlabru/issues/46
There it’s about how this interacts with the inlabru interface, but in solving that we
noted how things work in “raw” inla.

Finn
